Aloevera_Anthracnose.symptoms: Brown to dark necrotic lesions can develop on aloe leaves. Lesions may enlarge and cause localized tissue death and damaged leaf areas.
Aloevera_Anthracnose.management: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves. Keep the growing area clean, improve air circulation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Aloevera_Anthracnose.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation, provide adequate spacing and drainage, and remove infected plant debris.
Aloevera_Anthracnose.treatment_recommendations: Begin with sanitation and removal of infected tissue. If disease continues to spread, use only a fungicide registered for aloe and permitted for the intended use in your location, following its label.
Aloevera_Anthracnose.source: Shutrodhar & Shamsi, Anthracnose and leaf spot diseases of Aloe vera L., Dhaka University Journal of Biological Sciences (2013).
Aloevera_Anthracnose.treatment: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves and keep the growing area clean. Improve air circulation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness. If disease continues to spread, use only a fungicide that is registered and labelled for the crop and diagnosed disease in your area.

Aloevera_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have their normal green coloration and firm, healthy appearance, without significant necrotic lesions, abnormal spotting or disease-associated discoloration.
Aloevera_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain appropriate watering, drainage, sunlight and general plant hygiene.
Aloevera_Healthy.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid excessive moisture and inspect leaves regularly for newly developing spots or lesions.
Aloevera_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for a healthy plant. Continue normal cultural care and monitor for changes.
Aloevera_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; disease comparison based on Shutrodhar & Shamsi (2013).
Aloevera_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Continue normal Aloe vera care, including appropriate watering, drainage, light and sanitation. Monitor leaves regularly for new spots or lesions.

Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Localized leaf spots or lesions can develop and may enlarge or coalesce, producing brown or necrotic damaged areas.
Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove affected leaves, maintain sanitation, improve ventilation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid excessive leaf wetness and overhead irrigation, provide adequate spacing and remove infected plant material.
Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Remove infected tissue first. If disease pressure remains high, use a locally registered fungicide appropriate for aloe and follow the product label.
Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.source: Shutrodhar & Shamsi, Anthracnose and leaf spot diseases of Aloe vera L., Dhaka University Journal of Biological Sciences (2013).
Aloevera_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves and infected plant debris. Keep foliage as dry as practical and improve air circulation. For persistent disease, a locally registered fungicide may be considered according to its label and the confirmed causal organism.

Brahmi_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have normal green coloration and healthy tissue without obvious brown blight lesions, extensive necrosis or abnormal disease-associated damage.
Brahmi_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable moisture, drainage, nutrition and plant hygiene.
Brahmi_Healthy.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain sanitation and regularly inspect foliage.
Brahmi_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for a healthy plant. Continue normal cultivation and monitoring.
Brahmi_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; disease comparison based on published Bacopa monnieri leaf-blight research.
Brahmi_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable moisture, drainage, nutrition and sanitation, and monitor foliage regularly.

Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Leaf lesions can develop and enlarge, resulting in brown or necrotic blighted areas and progressive damage to the foliage.
Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove severely affected leaves, maintain sanitation, improve air circulation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid excessive moisture on foliage and remove infected plant material promptly.
Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Sanitation and removal of affected foliage should be the first measures. Biological control using Trichoderma has been investigated against Alternaria alternata causing Bacopa leaf blight.
Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.source: Identification and pathogenicity of Alternaria alternata causing leaf blight of Bacopa monnieri, Journal of Applied Research on Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (2022).
Brahmi_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves and plant debris. Improve air circulation and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. Because Alternaria leaf blight has been reported on Bacopa monnieri, disease management should follow locally recommended and crop-labelled plant-protection measures.

Camphor_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have their normal green coloration and healthy structure without significant necrotic spots, shot-hole lesions or abnormal discoloration.
Camphor_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain good plant vigor, drainage, sanitation and suitable growing conditions.
Camphor_Healthy.prevention: Maintain adequate air circulation and regularly inspect foliage for developing lesions or other abnormalities.
Camphor_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal plant care and monitoring.
Camphor_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; disease comparison based on published Cinnamomum camphora leaf-spot research.
Camphor_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain good plant vigor, appropriate watering and drainage, and inspect foliage regularly.

Camphor_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Leaf spots may begin as dark-green or water-soaked circular areas and progress to necrotic spots or shot-hole-like lesions surrounded by yellow halos.
Camphor_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove affected leaves, improve ventilation, reduce prolonged leaf wetness and maintain sanitation around the plant.
Camphor_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain suitable spacing and regularly inspect foliage.
Camphor_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves and improve canopy ventilation. If chemical treatment is required, use only a locally registered product appropriate for camphor and follow its label.
Camphor_Leaf_Spot.source: Li et al., First Report of Leaf Spot Disease on Cinnamomum camphora Caused by Epicoccum poaceicola, Plant Disease (2022).
Camphor_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove severely affected leaves and fallen infected material. Improve ventilation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness. If the disease persists, use only a locally registered fungicide appropriate for Cinnamomum camphora and the confirmed pathogen.

Harad_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves show normal green coloration and healthy tissue without significant leaf-spot lesions, necrosis or premature defoliation.
Harad_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain appropriate moisture, drainage, nutrition and sanitation.
Harad_Healthy.prevention: Use healthy planting material and inspect foliage regularly for developing lesions or abnormal discoloration.
Harad_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal cultivation and monitoring.
Harad_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; disease comparison based on published Terminalia chebula leaf-spot research.
Harad_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain healthy nursery conditions, appropriate moisture and sanitation, and monitor foliage.

Harad_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Leaf spots can develop on Terminalia chebula foliage and may become severe enough to cause extensive foliar damage and premature defoliation.
Harad_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove severely affected foliage, maintain sanitation and improve air circulation around plants.
Harad_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, monitor foliage regularly and remove infected plant debris.
Harad_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Use sanitation and removal of severely infected foliage as first measures. Chemical treatment should only use a plant-protection product registered for Terminalia and the intended use.
Harad_Leaf_Spot.source: Rajeshkumar et al., Pseudocercospora kamalii sp. nov., a foliar pathogen associated with severe leaf spot disease of Terminalia chebula, Mycotaxon (2011).
Harad_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves and infected debris and improve air circulation. For severe or persistent disease, obtain a proper diagnosis and follow locally recommended, crop-labelled fungicide or biological control measures.

Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.symptoms: Leaves show abnormal wrinkling, distortion or deformation compared with normal Hibiscus foliage.
Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.management: Inspect affected plants for additional disease, pest or environmental symptoms. Remove severely damaged leaves and maintain good plant hygiene.
Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.prevention: Regularly monitor new foliage and maintain suitable water, nutrition, drainage and growing conditions.
Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.treatment_recommendations: Wrinkling alone does not establish a specific pathogen. Identify the underlying cause before applying a pesticide or fungicide; remove severely damaged foliage where appropriate.
Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.source: Dataset-defined Hibiscus leaf-condition class. Wrinkling should not be treated as a confirmed pathogen diagnosis without further diagnosis.
Hibiscus_ Wrinkled_Leaf.treatment: Do not apply a disease treatment based on leaf wrinkling alone because wrinkling can have different causes. Inspect the plant for insects, virus-like symptoms, nutritional problems and environmental stress. Remove severely damaged leaves and seek diagnosis if the condition continues.

Hibiscus_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves show normal green coloration and normal leaf structure without significant disease-associated spots, necrosis, severe deformation or abnormal discoloration.
Hibiscus_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain adequate water, nutrition, drainage, light and plant hygiene.
Hibiscus_Healthy.prevention: Regularly inspect foliage and maintain good growing conditions. Remove diseased plant material if symptoms appear.
Hibiscus_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal plant care and monitoring.
Hibiscus_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class. UC IPM recognizes leaf spot diseases among diseases affecting Hibiscus.
Hibiscus_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain appropriate watering, nutrition, light, drainage and sanitation. Continue regular inspection of the foliage.

Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Leaf spots may be circular or irregular and can develop dark borders, chlorotic halos or necrotic centers. Severe spotting may cause premature leaf drop.
Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove affected leaves, maintain sanitation, reduce prolonged leaf wetness and improve air circulation.
Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation where possible, maintain adequate spacing and drainage, and remove infected plant debris.
Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Improve moisture management and remove severely affected foliage. If a chemical treatment is needed, use a locally registered product appropriate for the identified disease and host.
Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.source: UC IPM Hibiscus disease-management information and University of Hawaii CTAHR bacterial leaf-spot guidance.
Hibiscus_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove affected leaves and fallen diseased debris and avoid overhead watering. Improve airflow and keep foliage dry when practical. If disease is severe, use a fungicide specifically labelled for Hibiscus and the diagnosed disease. Fungicides should be used according to the product label.

Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Small dark or water-soaked lesions can develop on leaves and may enlarge, become necrotic and damage surrounding leaf tissue.
Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove severely affected foliage, maintain sanitation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid unnecessary leaf wetness, maintain spacing and remove infected plant debris.
Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Prioritize sanitation and moisture management. Because this is a bacterial disease, fungicides should not be assumed to be effective; use only a bactericide or other product specifically registered for the crop and disease.
Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.source: MoringaLeafNet: A multi-class leaf disease dataset for precision agriculture and deep learning research (2025).
Moringa_Bacterial_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove and destroy severely affected leaves and infected plant debris. Avoid unnecessary leaf wetness and overhead irrigation and maintain good field sanitation. If bacterial disease is confirmed and severe, consult local agricultural recommendations before applying any bactericide.

Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Small leaf lesions can develop and enlarge, producing characteristic spotted and damaged areas of leaf tissue.
Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove severely affected leaves, maintain sanitation, provide adequate spacing and reduce prolonged moisture on foliage.
Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain good field sanitation and remove infected plant debris.
Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Use sanitation and moisture management first. If fungicide treatment is required, use only a product registered for Moringa and Cercospora leaf spot in your jurisdiction.
Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.source: MoringaLeafNet: A multi-class leaf disease dataset for precision agriculture and deep learning research (2025).
Moringa_Cercospora_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and plant debris and maintain good sanitation. Improve airflow and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. For severe disease, use only a fungicide registered for Moringa and the confirmed disease according to its label.

Moringa_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have normal green coloration and healthy tissue without significant yellowing, leaf spots or necrotic lesions.
Moringa_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable water, nutrition, drainage and plant hygiene.
Moringa_Healthy.prevention: Regularly inspect foliage and remove diseased plant material if symptoms develop.
Moringa_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal cultivation and monitoring.
Moringa_Healthy.source: Healthy Leaf is one of the four documented MoringaLeafNet classes.
Moringa_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable irrigation, nutrition, drainage and sanitation. Monitor leaves regularly for spotting or abnormal yellowing.

Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.symptoms: Leaves develop abnormal yellowing or chlorosis affecting part or much of the leaf.
Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.management: Inspect the plant for possible disease, nutrient or environmental causes. Maintain appropriate irrigation and nutrition and remove severely affected material.
Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.prevention: Monitor leaf color regularly and maintain balanced nutrition, suitable moisture and good growing conditions.
Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.treatment_recommendations: Yellowing is a symptom rather than a single confirmed cause. Determine whether disease, nutrient deficiency, water stress or another factor is responsible before applying treatment.
Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.source: MoringaLeafNet: A multi-class leaf disease dataset for precision agriculture and deep learning research (2025).
Moringa_Yellow_Leaf.treatment: Yellowing is not specific to one disease and may result from nutrient deficiency, water stress, root problems or disease. Do not apply a disease treatment solely from the image classification. Check soil moisture, drainage, nutrition and roots and obtain a diagnosis if yellowing persists.

Neem_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves show normal green coloration and healthy tissue without significant spots, lesions, necrosis or abnormal discoloration.
Neem_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable growing conditions, drainage and plant sanitation.
Neem_Healthy.prevention: Regularly inspect foliage and maintain good plant health and sanitation.
Neem_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal care and monitoring.
Neem_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; comparison based on documented Neem foliar disease literature.
Neem_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable growing conditions, adequate drainage and plant sanitation. Continue regular foliage inspection.

Neem_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Brown to dark leaf lesions or spots can occur on neem foliage and may enlarge or coalesce under favorable conditions.
Neem_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove severely affected leaves, maintain sanitation and improve air circulation.
Neem_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid prolonged leaf wetness, maintain plant hygiene and monitor foliage regularly.
Neem_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Remove infected foliage and improve environmental conditions. Where disease persists, use only a locally registered fungicide appropriate for neem and the diagnosed pathogen.
Neem_Leaf_Spot.source: Published reports of foliar leaf spot diseases of Azadirachta indica, including Cercospora-associated leaf spot.
Neem_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove severely affected leaves and infected plant debris and improve air circulation. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness. For severe disease, use only a locally registered fungicide appropriate for Neem and the confirmed leaf-spot pathogen.

Patharchatta_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves are normally green, fleshy and intact, without significant brown or black lesions, necrosis or disease-associated damage.
Patharchatta_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable drainage, watering and general plant hygiene.
Patharchatta_Healthy.prevention: Avoid excessive moisture, provide suitable ventilation and inspect succulent leaves regularly.
Patharchatta_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal care and monitoring.
Patharchatta_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; disease comparison based on published Kalanchoe pinnata leaf-spot research.
Patharchatta_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain good drainage and avoid excessive watering. Keep the plant area clean and monitor the succulent leaves for lesions.

Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Brown to black irregular lesions can develop, often near leaf margins. Lesions may enlarge and coalesce into larger damaged areas.
Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.management: Remove affected leaves, maintain sanitation and reduce prolonged leaf wetness.
Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Avoid excessive humidity around foliage, maintain good ventilation and remove infected plant debris.
Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.treatment_recommendations: Remove affected foliage and improve ventilation and moisture management. Further chemical treatment should follow local registration and diagnosis.
Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.source: Sun et al., First Report of Diaporthe longicolla Causing Leaf Spot on Kalanchoe pinnata, Plant Disease (2021).
Patharchatta_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Remove affected leaves and infected plant debris. Avoid excessive humidity and prolonged leaf wetness and improve ventilation. If disease continues, seek diagnosis and use only a locally registered treatment appropriate for Kalanchoe and the confirmed pathogen.

Piper_Betal_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves show normal green coloration and healthy structure without significant brown spots, yellow halos, necrotic lesions or rot.
Piper_Betal_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable humidity, drainage, ventilation and sanitation.
Piper_Betal_Healthy.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain the growing area clean and inspect leaves regularly.
Piper_Betal_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal betel-vine cultivation and monitoring.
Piper_Betal_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; comparison based on documented Piper betle disease literature.
Piper_Betal_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable humidity, drainage, ventilation and sanitation. Monitor foliage regularly.

Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Irregular or circular light-to-dark brown spots may develop, sometimes surrounded by yellow halos. Lesions can enlarge and cause yellowing, drying and drooping.
Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove infected leaves, improve ventilation, reduce prolonged leaf wetness and maintain sanitation.
Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid excessive leaf wetness, maintain suitable spacing and regularly remove infected plant material.
Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Remove affected foliage and improve sanitation and ventilation. Specific fungicide treatment should be based on diagnosis and locally registered recommendations.
Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.source: Shabong & Kayang, First report of Diaporthe tulliensis causing leaf spot of betel vine, New Disease Reports (2023).
Piper_Betal_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and maintain strict sanitation. Improve ventilation and reduce prolonged leaf wetness. Biological management such as Bacillus subtilis has been investigated for betelvine leaf-spot disease. Chemical treatment should only use products registered and labelled for betelvine and the confirmed disease.

Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.symptoms: Leaves may develop yellowing associated with disease-related spotting or tissue damage, particularly when lesions expand and affected tissue dries.
Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.management: Inspect for associated leaf-spot, rot or other disease symptoms. Remove affected leaves and improve sanitation, ventilation and moisture management.
Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.prevention: Maintain suitable moisture, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and monitor leaves regularly.
Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.treatment_recommendations: Yellowing is a symptom and does not identify one disease by itself. Inspect the plant for the underlying cause before applying treatment.
Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.source: Piper betle disease literature; leaf-spot disease with associated yellowing is documented by Shabong & Kayang (2023).
Piper_Betal_Yellow_Leaf.treatment: Leaf yellowing is not specific to one disease. Inspect the plant for associated leaf spot, rot, root problems, water stress and nutritional problems before selecting a treatment. Correct the underlying problem and remove severely affected leaves.

Tamarind_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have normal green coloration and healthy tissue without significant leaf spots, powdery fungal growth or necrotic lesions.
Tamarind_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain good plant vigor, sanitation, drainage and suitable growing conditions.
Tamarind_Healthy.prevention: Regularly inspect foliage and remove diseased plant material if symptoms develop.
Tamarind_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal plant care and monitoring.
Tamarind_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; comparison based on documented Tamarindus indica disease literature.
Tamarind_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain good plant vigor, suitable drainage, sanitation and regular foliage monitoring.

Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Leaf spots may be pale brown to golden brown, subcircular or irregular, and may enlarge or coalesce.
Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove affected foliage, maintain sanitation and improve air circulation.
Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Remove infected plant debris, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and regularly monitor foliage.
Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Begin with removal of affected foliage and sanitation. Chemical control should be based on confirmed diagnosis and locally registered products.
Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.source: Pseudocercospora tamarindi literature documenting leaf spots on Tamarindus indica.
Tamarind_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove affected leaves and infected plant debris and improve air circulation. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness. For severe disease, obtain confirmation of the causal organism and use only a locally registered fungicide labelled for Tamarind and that disease.

Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth can develop on leaf surfaces and may become more extensive as infection progresses.
Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.management: Remove severely infected leaves, improve air circulation and reduce conditions favoring prolonged humidity.
Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.prevention: Maintain suitable spacing and ventilation, monitor foliage regularly and remove infected material.
Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.treatment_recommendations: Remove severely infected foliage and improve ventilation. If treatment is necessary, use a locally registered fungicide specifically recommended for powdery mildew on the crop.
Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.source: Foliage fungal disease survey reporting Oidium tamarindi on Tamarindus indica.
Tamarind_Powdery_Mildew.treatment: Remove severely infected leaves and improve air circulation around the plant. Avoid excessive humidity and overcrowding. If treatment is required, use only a fungicide registered and labelled for powdery mildew on the crop and follow the product label.

Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.symptoms: Yellow or chlorotic areas may appear on the upper leaf surface, while gray to purple-brown sporulation may develop on the underside of affected areas.
Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.management: Remove affected leaves or plants, improve air movement and reduce leaf wetness and humidity.
Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain ventilation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and inspect both leaf surfaces regularly.
Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.treatment_recommendations: Use an integrated approach involving sanitation, reduced leaf wetness, ventilation and resistant varieties where available. Chemical treatment should only use products registered for the specific crop and disease.
Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.source: American Phytopathological Society diagnostic and management literature for basil downy mildew caused by Peronospora belbahrii.
Tulsi_Downy_Mildew.treatment: Remove severely infected leaves or plants and reduce leaf wetness and humidity around the foliage. Improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation. Use disease-resistant planting material where available. For severe disease, use only a fungicide specifically registered and labelled for the crop and downy mildew in your region.

Tulsi_Healthy.plant: Tulsi / Holy basil (Ocimum sanctum / Ocimum tenuiflorum)
Tulsi_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves show normal coloration and healthy structure without significant leaf spots, mildew growth, severe wilting or abnormal disease-associated discoloration.
Tulsi_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable watering, drainage, nutrition, ventilation and plant hygiene.
Tulsi_Healthy.prevention: Regularly inspect leaves and maintain good growing conditions and sanitation.
Tulsi_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal cultivation and monitoring.
Tulsi_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; comparison based on documented Ocimum disease literature.
Tulsi_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain appropriate watering, drainage, nutrition, ventilation and sanitation. Continue monitoring the leaves.

Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.plant: Tulsi / Holy basil (Ocimum sanctum / Ocimum tenuiflorum)
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Brown or necrotic leaf lesions can develop and may enlarge or coalesce, causing damaged leaf tissue.
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.management: Remove affected leaves, maintain sanitation, improve air circulation and reduce prolonged leaf wetness.
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.prevention: Avoid unnecessary overhead irrigation, maintain suitable spacing and monitor foliage regularly.
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.treatment_recommendations: Remove infected foliage and improve environmental conditions. Published research has investigated Trichoderma and plant-extract-based biological approaches against leaf-spot pathogens of Ocimum sanctum; chemical treatment should follow local registration.
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.source: Research documenting leaf spot of Ocimum sanctum, including Colletotrichum and Neopestalotiopsis chrysea.
Tulsi_Leaf_Spot.treatment: Remove affected leaves and infected debris and improve air circulation. Avoid prolonged leaf wetness and overhead irrigation. If disease is severe, use only a locally registered fungicide labelled for Ocimum and the confirmed leaf-spot disease.

Turmeric_Healthy.symptoms: Leaves have normal green coloration and healthy tissue without significant leaf spots, blotches, abnormal yellowing or scorched areas.
Turmeric_Healthy.management: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable irrigation, drainage, nutrition and field sanitation.
Turmeric_Healthy.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain field sanitation and monitor foliage regularly.
Turmeric_Healthy.treatment_recommendations: No treatment is required for healthy foliage. Continue normal crop management and monitoring.
Turmeric_Healthy.source: Healthy condition defined as the disease-free reference class; comparison based on Kerala Agricultural University and Tamil Nadu Agricultural University turmeric disease resources.
Turmeric_Healthy.treatment: No disease treatment is required. Maintain suitable irrigation, drainage, nutrition and field sanitation. Continue monitoring the foliage for early signs of disease.

Turmeric_leaf_spot.symptoms: Elliptical or oblong spots with yellow halos may develop. Spot centers can become grayish or straw-colored and severely affected leaves may dry and develop a scorched appearance.
Turmeric_leaf_spot.management: Remove and destroy severely infected leaves or plants, maintain field sanitation and reduce conditions that favor prolonged leaf wetness.
Turmeric_leaf_spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, maintain field sanitation, avoid excessive moisture on foliage and monitor plants regularly.
Turmeric_leaf_spot.treatment_recommendations: Follow locally approved turmeric disease-management recommendations. KAU and TNAU describe sanitation and registered fungicide options for turmeric leaf spot; use any pesticide strictly according to the current local label.
Turmeric_leaf_spot.source: Kerala Agricultural University and Tamil Nadu Agricultural University turmeric leaf-spot disease-management resources.
Turmeric_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves and plant debris and maintain proper plant spacing. Use healthy planting material and avoid prolonged leaf wetness. For significant disease, locally recommended fungicides may be used only according to the current product label and agricultural recommendations.
